summary: Stale balances are most likely caused by the config change cfg-holdings-cache-ttl at 12:00 UTC, which raised portfolio-svc's HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S from 60 to 1800. After that change portfolio-svc served holdings from cache with entry ages climbing to 1800s, and cache_staleness_s peaked at 1800. The update pipeline looks healthy: portfolio-updates depth is 0 with no DLQ, and consume rate matches publish rate. Redis is healthy with no evictions, so the past redis-restart incident (INC-0412) does not apply. Stale reads of up to 30 minutes match the reports that trades older than ten minutes are missing.

hypotheses.statement: The HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S increase from 60 to 1800 on portfolio-svc made holdings cache entries live up to 30 minutes. Reads therefore return stale balances even though the update pipeline is delivering data on time.
hypotheses.label: high

unresolved: The cache log query was truncated (68 matches, 30 returned), so I did not see every log line after 12:11.
I did not confirm that portfolio-consumer writes invalidate or refresh the holdings cache. If they do not, even the old 60s TTL would show some staleness.
I did not check the exact time the first user reports began relative to 12:00. The staleness window only exceeds ten minutes from about 12:10 onward.

actions.text: Revert HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S to 60 on portfolio-svc, then invalidate or flush the holdings cache keys so existing 1800s entries stop being served.
actions.rationale: The TTL change at 12:00 matches the observed entry ages and staleness of 1800s. The pipeline is healthy, so the cache is the only layer holding old data.

actions.text: After the revert, confirm that cache_staleness_s drops back to roughly 60s or less and that users see fresh balances.
actions.rationale: This verifies the fix against the same metric that showed the problem.

actions.text: Find out why the TTL change was made and add a review guard for cache TTL changes on balance data. Consider invalidating cache entries when portfolio-consumer applies an update.
actions.rationale: A longer TTL is only safe if writes invalidate cached holdings.
